results.text:
**Plan.** I will estimate the effect of turnout on the incumbent party's county vote share by two-stage least squares, instrumenting county turnout with `eday_rain` (election-day rainfall deviation from the county's 1948–2000 election-day mean) in a panel of ~3,100 counties × 14 elections with county and election-year fixed effects and standard errors clustered by state. Key variables are the outcome (incumbent-party vote share, pp), the treatment (turnout, pp of voting-age population), the instrument `eday_rain`, the fixed effects, and `dem_prev`, `pop_density`, `pct_rural`, `median_inc`, and `south` used as precision controls and for balance tests (rainfall deviations should be uncorrelated with them conditional on the fixed effects). The first stage is strong (about −1.1 pp turnout per inch; I will report the first-stage F), and because within-county deviations in election-day rain are plausibly as-good-as-random, independence is credible. The main threat is the exclusion restriction: rain could move the incumbent's share through channels other than turnout—weather-driven mood or local economic/flood shocks that color evaluations of the incumbent—and the estimate is a LATE for rain-sensitive marginal voters rather than the average turnout effect, so I will run placebo tests using rainfall on adjacent non-election days, check that `eday_rain` does not predict `dem_prev` or the covariates conditional on fixed effects, and probe heterogeneity by `south` and over time given changes in polling hours and absentee rules. I considered `reminder_draw`, which is a clean randomized nonpartisan mailing with a credible exclusion restriction, but it covers only 180 county-elections with a 0.3 pp first stage and F ≈ 4, so 2SLS with it would be badly biased toward OLS; I will use it only as a secondary Anderson–Rubin (weak-IV-robust) check, not as the main instrument. The remaining codebook variables (demographic/political controls and the agency survey/administrative items, many of which are collected only in odd-numbered years or post-2013 and so are not even measured for presidential election years) are not valid instruments.

CANDIDATES:
eday_rain | plausible
reminder_draw | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: eday_rain

**Plan.** With no credible instrument available (see below), I would use the four-round panel as the design: regress four-week illness episodes on log household income per adult equivalent with individual and survey-round fixed effects, cluster standard errors at the village level (51 clusters), and include season_rain (and its wet-season indicator) as a village-round control so the weather shocks that move both income and disease are absorbed rather than exploited, stating plainly that this identifies the effect only from within-person income changes net of common shocks and is not a fully causal estimate. As the sole experimental evidence I would report the reduced-form intention-to-treat effect of transfer_draw on illness in the 6 pilot villages, using randomization inference over the 20 possible draws of 3 villages and pre-1993 rounds as placebo, but not as an instrument. Key variables are illness episodes (outcome), log income (treatment), season_rain, transfer_draw, and age, female, educ_years, hh_size, dist_clinic and land_acres as baseline covariates; the roughly 300 generically labelled variables (househ_numb_000 through assets_chan_299) cite 2013–2015 system changes, nominal dollars and CPI-U deflation that cannot apply to a 1991–94 Tanzanian household survey, so I would exclude them regardless of the PI's cleaning. I reject IV because season_rain, despite a strong first stage (0.08 log points per 100 mm), violates the exclusion restriction—the health office documents malaria rising after every wet season, so rain changes illness directly, not only through income—while transfer_draw is randomized and excludable but, with 3 treated villages, a 0.02 log-point income shift and a first-stage F of about 2, is far too weak: 2SLS would be biased toward OLS and weak-IV-robust (Anderson–Rubin) confidence sets would be essentially unbounded. The main threat to the fixed-effects estimate is reverse causality and time-varying confounding—illness in the recall window itself reduces income, and unmeasured local shocks (outbreaks, price changes) move both—so the result should be read as an association with a likely overstated negative effect, and I would advise the PI to seek stronger exogenous income variation before making a causal claim.

CANDIDATES:
transfer_draw | doubtful
season_rain | violated
land_acres | violated
dist_clinic | violated
INSTRUMENT: NONE

**Plan.** I will estimate the effect of county turnout on the incumbent party's vote share by instrumental variables, using the randomized mailed-reminder draw (`reminder_draw`) as the instrument for turnout within the 180 county-elections of the 1996–2000 three-state pilot, with election-year (or state-by-year) fixed effects and the pre-treatment covariates (`dem_prev`, `pop_density`, `pct_rural`, `median_inc`, `south`) included only for precision. Because the draw was random within election year, the mailing named no candidate or party, and nothing else changed in drawn counties, independence and the exclusion restriction hold by design, and the estimand is a LATE for voters mobilized by the reminder in those states and years. I reject `eday_rain` despite its strong first stage (−1.1 pp turnout per inch): the election offices' post-election surveys show that people who voted on wet polling days were more risk-averse and chose the incumbent party's candidate more often than voters with the same voting history, so rain shifts the outcome directly through vote choice rather than only through turnout, which violates exclusion. The remaining codebook items (the generic `religi_*`, `employ_*`, `educat_*`, etc. agency fields) have no first-stage rationale for turnout and are not instrument candidates regardless of how clean they are. The main threat is weak identification: a 0.3 pp first stage with F ≈ 4 means 2SLS is biased toward OLS and conventional standard errors are invalid, so I will report the reduced form and Anderson–Rubin (identification-robust) confidence sets instead of 2SLS t-statistics, clustered by county, and pre-commit that an unbounded or very wide AR set is reported as "uninformative" rather than replaced by the rain instrument. Secondary limitations are the small sample and external validity confined to the three pilot states in 1996–2000.

CANDIDATES:
eday_rain | violated
reminder_draw | plausible
INSTRUMENT: reminder_draw

Neither candidate instrument supports a credible IV design: season_rain has a strong first stage (0.08 log points per 100 mm) but fails the exclusion restriction, because the health office's surveillance records show above-average rainfall raises malaria cases and therefore illness episodes directly, while transfer_draw is genuinely randomized but moves log income by only 0.02 with a first-stage F of about 2 and three treated villages out of six, so 2SLS would be biased toward OLS with essentially uninformative inference. I will therefore estimate a within-person panel design: illness episodes in the past four weeks regressed on log household income per adult equivalent with individual and survey-round fixed effects, a second specification adding village-by-round fixed effects to absorb common local shocks such as rainfall, and standard errors clustered at the village level (51 clusters). Key variables are the outcome (illness episodes), the treatment (log income per adult equivalent), time-varying controls age and hh_size, and season_rain and transfer_draw used only as diagnostics; the generically labeled variables (househ_numb_000 through assets_chan_299) reference a 2013 system migration, 2014 definition changes, and CPI-U dollars, so they cannot belong to a 1991-94 Tanzanian village survey and I will not use them despite the note that they are cleaned. As supplementary, explicitly underpowered checks I will report the reduced-form intention-to-treat effect of transfer_draw on illness episodes within the six pilot villages using randomization inference over the 20 possible assignments, and I will test whether season_rain predicts illness conditional on income as a direct confirmation of the exclusion violation. The main threat to the fixed-effects estimate is reverse causality and contemporaneous shocks: an illness during the recall window lowers that period's income through lost labor and medical spending, and weather or price shocks move both income and health, so the within-person estimate must be reported as an association whose likely bias (toward finding that income protects health) is stated explicitly rather than as a causal effect.

CANDIDATES:
transfer_draw | doubtful
season_rain | violated
dist_clinic | violated
land_acres | doubtful
educ_years | violated
INSTRUMENT: NONE

**Plan.** I would not run an instrumental-variables design as the main analysis, because neither candidate instrument in the codebook can credibly identify the effect of rural income growth on riots: monsoon_dev has a strong first stage (10 points of rainfall deviation raises rural income growth by 1.6 pp), but the exclusion restriction is directly contradicted by the police registers, which show that canal-irrigated districts downstream of dams, whose crop income does not move with the monsoon, record about the same rise in riots in deficit-monsoon years as other districts, so rainfall shocks reach riots through channels other than income (heat, water disputes, relief politics). works_draw is a genuine lottery with a plausible exclusion restriction ("the program changed nothing else"), but it covers only 16 districts in one state in 1993-1995, shifts income growth by just 0.2 pp, and has a first-stage F of about 2, so 2SLS would be biased toward OLS and Anderson-Rubin confidence sets would be essentially uninformative. The main design would therefore be a district fixed-effects panel: regress the riot count (PPML or negative binomial with district and year fixed effects, state-by-year fixed effects, lagged riots, and year effects interacted with the 1981 covariates pop_1981, muslim_share, urban_share, literacy, and riots_prev) on annual rural income growth, with standard errors clustered by district, stated explicitly as identified only under a parallel-trends/selection-on-observables assumption rather than as a clean causal effect. As supplementary evidence I would report the works_draw reduced form (ITT of the program on riots) with randomization inference over the 16 districts, and I would present the dam-district contrast as a falsification test showing why the monsoon IV is invalid rather than reporting its 2SLS estimate. The main threat is reverse causality and time-varying district-year confounders (riots depress local economic activity, and political mobilization, elections, or policing shocks move both income and riots), which fixed effects cannot remove. The remaining generic codebook variables (wage_*, crop_*, price_*, etc.) are not usable instruments: their documentation (nominal dollars, a 2013 system migration, a 2014 vendor change, odd-year collection) is anachronistic for 1982-1995 Indian districts and none has a plausible exclusion restriction.

CANDIDATES:
monsoon_dev | violated
works_draw | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

I will estimate the effect of rural income growth on riots by two-stage least squares with district and year fixed effects, instrumenting annual district rural income growth with monsoon_dev (percent deviation of June–September rainfall from the district's 1951–1980 mean), so identification comes from within-district, year-to-year rainfall shocks that are plausibly as-good-as-random once permanent district differences and nationwide shocks are absorbed, with a strong first stage (a 10-point deviation raises growth by 1.6 percentage points). The key variables are the riot count (outcome), rural income growth (treatment), monsoon_dev (instrument), district and year fixed effects, and the 1981 covariates (pop_1981, muslim_share, urban_share, literacy, riots_prev) and state, which are absorbed by district effects but will be interacted with year dummies as robustness controls and used for heterogeneity (e.g., effects by muslim_share and urban_share). I will cluster standard errors by district (checking state clustering), report the reduced form of riots on monsoon_dev alongside OLS and 2SLS, and, because riots are a count with many zeros, complement linear 2SLS with a control-function Poisson and a 2SLS on an any-riot indicator, also testing lagged growth and lagged rainfall. The main threat is the exclusion restriction: rainfall could affect riots through channels other than income (floods or droughts changing mobility, gatherings, policing, or migration), and the income effect may be nonlinear (both droughts and floods lower income), so I will use flexible rainfall functional forms (deviation bins or absolute deviation) as over-identifying checks, verify that positive and negative shocks operate symmetrically through income, and show that rainfall does not predict riots where agriculture matters little (high urban_share). I will not use works_draw as an instrument: although the 1992 draw was random and plausibly excludable, it covers only 16 districts in one state over 1993–1995 (about 48 observations) with a 0.2-point first stage and an F-statistic near 2, so it fails the relevance condition and 2SLS on it would be severely biased toward OLS with uninformative confidence intervals; at most I will report its reduced form as a descriptive check. The remaining agency/vendor variables (wage_*, crop_*, price_*, police_*, etc.) describe 2013–2014 system migrations, nominal dollars, CPI-U deflation and probabilistic person-level linkage, none of which fit 1982–1995 Indian district data, so I treat them as unusable for this design rather than as instruments or controls.

CANDIDATES:
monsoon_dev | plausible
works_draw | violated
INSTRUMENT: monsoon_dev

The only exogenous variation in rural income growth that the codebook documents credibly is the 1992 public-works lottery (works_draw), so the plan treats the 8 drawn versus 8 undrawn districts in 1993-1995 as a randomized experiment: estimate the reduced-form effect of the draw on the district-year riot count with district and year fixed effects, use randomization inference over the 12,870 possible 8-of-16 assignments, and report an Anderson-Rubin confidence set for the effect of income growth rather than a 2SLS point estimate. Key variables are the riot count (outcome), annual rural income growth in percent (treatment), works_draw (exogenous shifter), and pop_1981, muslim_share, urban_share, literacy and riots_prev used only as balance checks, not as controls that carry the identification. monsoon_dev is rejected despite its strong first stage (10 points of rainfall deviation moves income growth 1.6 pp) because the codebook reports that canal-irrigated districts, whose crop income does not move with the monsoon, show the same rise in riots in dry years as other districts, which means rainfall affects riots through channels other than income and the exclusion restriction fails. The main threat is that works_draw is weak: a 0.2 pp first stage with F of about 2 in roughly 48 district-years means 2SLS would be biased toward OLS with unreliable standard errors, and the AR set will likely be wide or unbounded, so the honest deliverable is a clean intention-to-treat effect of the program on riots plus a statement that this dataset cannot pin down the income effect itself. The remaining codebook variables (wage_*, crop_*, police_*, etc.) describe no assignment mechanism and carry documentation inconsistent with 1982-1995 India (nominal dollars, CPI-U, 2013-2014 system changes), so none is a candidate instrument and none should be used without reconciling the documentation. Because no available variable is both excludable and strong, I would not present an instrumented estimate as the headline result; if the PI wants a credible income effect, the next step is to obtain the dam/canal-command indicator referenced in the memo so the monsoon's direct effect can be differenced out across canal and non-canal districts.

CANDIDATES:
monsoon_dev | violated
works_draw | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

Identification strategy: neither candidate instrument supports a credible 2SLS, so I will not use IV; the main specification is a within-individual fixed-effects regression of illness episodes on log household income per adult equivalent with survey-round and village-by-round fixed effects, standard errors clustered at the village level (51 clusters), presented explicitly as a conditional association rather than a clean causal estimate.

season_rain has a genuine first stage (0.08 log points per 100 mm) but rainfall in the months before the interview directly alters malaria, diarrheal-disease and flooding exposure in the four-week recall window, so it violates the exclusion restriction and would load rainfall's direct health effects onto income.

transfer_draw is randomized and excludable ("the fund changed nothing else"), but a first stage of 0.02 with F≈2 from 3 treated versus 3 control villages would make 2SLS badly biased toward OLS with uninformative weak-IV-robust intervals, so I will only report its reduced-form intention-to-treat effect on illness with village-level randomization inference (20 possible assignments) as a transparent but underpowered check.

Key variables: the outcome (illness episodes, four-week recall), the treatment (log income per adult equivalent), individual, round and village×round fixed effects, and age and hh_size as time-varying controls; I will not use the roughly 300 auto-generated variables, since their documentation (2013 system migration, 2014 definition changes, CPI-U dollar deflation, state data warehouse extracts) cannot describe a 1991–1994 Tanzanian household survey and they need to be verified before any use.

Main threat: reverse causality and simultaneity — illness during the recall window cuts labor supply and income in the same round, biasing the fixed-effects estimate toward a protective income effect — so I will re-estimate with the previous round's income and interpret the gap between the two as the plausible size of this bias.

CANDIDATES:
season_rain | violated
transfer_draw | doubtful
dist_clinic | violated
land_acres | violated
INSTRUMENT: NONE

Neither candidate instrument supports a credible IV design: `waterways` has a strong first stage, but the codebook itself states the mechanism—streams became school-district and municipal boundaries—so waterways shift per-resident spending directly through jurisdictional fragmentation (Tiebout competition, duplicated or unshared services), violating the exclusion restriction; `audit_grant` is randomly assigned and plausibly excludable, but it is a weak instrument (first-stage F ≈ 2, a 0.3-point shift) observed in only 40 cities in two states, so 2SLS would be biased toward OLS and Anderson-Rubin confidence sets would be effectively uninformative.

I will therefore estimate a within-city panel design: regress CPI-deflated direct general expenditure per resident on the multigroup entropy index with city fixed effects and state-by-year fixed effects, so identification comes from changes in a city's own segregation across 1980, 1990, 2000 and 2010 relative to other cities in the same state and decade.

Controls are log_pop, pct_black, pct_hisp, med_income and own_rate, with standard errors clustered by city, plus a long-difference specification and a check that lagged changes in spending do not predict later changes in segregation (reverse causality and pre-trends).

As a design-based complement, I will report the randomized reduced form of `audit_grant` on spending among the 40 eligible cities using randomization inference, understanding that it identifies the grant's total effect, is badly underpowered, and cannot be scaled into a credible per-point effect of segregation.

The main threat is time-varying city shocks—industrial decline, white flight, erosion of the tax base, changes in state aid—that move both segregation and spending within a city and are not absorbed by fixed effects, so the estimate must be presented as a fixed-effects association with explicit sensitivity bounds rather than as a clean causal effect.

The roughly 300 generic "items" variables (odd-year collection, 2013–2015 system changes, matching on date of birth) do not correspond to the decennial city panel and will not be used.

CANDIDATES:
waterways | violated
audit_grant | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

Identification will come from the randomized 1996–2000 reminder pilot: I will estimate the effect of county turnout (percentage points of voting-age population) on the incumbent party's county vote share by 2SLS on the 180 pilot county-elections, instrumenting turnout with reminder_draw and including election-year and state indicators (the strata of the draw) plus dem_prev as a pre-determined precision covariate. Because the draw was random and the reminder was nonpartisan and changed nothing else in drawn counties, independence and exclusion hold by design, so the estimate is a credible local effect of turnout among voters nudged by the reminder rather than a regression with controls. I will not use eday_rain despite its strong first stage, because the survey evidence shows rain makes people who still vote more risk-averse and more pro-incumbent, a direct channel from the instrument to the outcome that violates the exclusion restriction and would wrongly attribute a pro-incumbent rain effect to lower turnout. The main threat is weak identification: the reminder raises turnout only 0.3 points with a first-stage F of about 4, so conventional 2SLS point estimates are biased toward OLS and their standard errors understate uncertainty; I will therefore report the reduced-form effect of the draw on incumbent share and Anderson–Rubin confidence sets as the primary inference, and commit to reporting the set as-is even if it is very wide or uninformative rather than falling back on rain. The result applies to three states in 1996–2000 and should not be extrapolated to the full 1948–2000 panel; fixed-effects OLS on the full panel with dem_prev, pop_density, pct_rural, median_inc, and south can be shown only as a descriptive benchmark. None of the remaining codebook items (generic survey and administrative fields) plausibly shift turnout while being excludable from the vote-share equation, so they are not instrument candidates.

CANDIDATES:
eday_rain | violated
reminder_draw | plausible
INSTRUMENT: reminder_draw

I will instrument the segregation index with audit_grant, the 1990 federal random draw among the 40 cities over 100,000 residents in the two participating states, estimating 2SLS on those cities in the post-draw census years (1990, 2000, 2010) with city direct general expenditure per resident as the outcome, controls for log_pop, pct_black, pct_hisp, med_income and own_rate, state-by-year effects, and inference clustered by city. Randomization makes the draw independent of city characteristics, and because the grant paid a nonprofit rather than the city government and changed nothing else in drawn cities, the exclusion restriction is credible, so the reduced-form effect of the draw on spending is a clean intention-to-treat estimate and the IV estimate is the effect of segregation for complier cities. I reject waterways despite its strong first stage (1.5 points per waterway): every counted stream was a boundary stream in the 1920 survey that became a jurisdiction line, so waterways directly raises the number of separately governed municipalities and school districts, and that fragmentation affects city spending through Tiebout competition and cost-sharing independently of segregation, which violates exclusion. The main threat is weak-instrument bias and low power: a first-stage F of about 2 and a 0.3-point first stage across only 40 cities mean conventional 2SLS is biased toward OLS and its standard errors are unreliable, so I will report Anderson-Rubin confidence sets and the reduced form as the primary results and accept that they may be wide or unbounded. Within-city fixed-effects regressions on the full 2,600-city panel will be shown only as descriptive benchmarks, not causal estimates, because changes in segregation are endogenous to the same demographic and fiscal processes that drive spending.

CANDIDATES:
waterways | violated
audit_grant | plausible
INSTRUMENT: audit_grant

Neither randomized variable in the codebook gives a credible instrument for high-school graduation: preschool_assign is random with a strong first stage (19 pp) but violates the exclusion restriction, because the program also reduced externalizing behavior and raised academic motivation, and those psychosocial skills independently raise adult turnout by 11-14 pp, so a 2SLS coefficient on graduation would absorb that direct channel. credit_waiver plausibly satisfies exclusion (random draw, "changed nothing else") but exists only for the few 1965-wave students who reached 12th grade and has a 4 pp first stage with F of about 2, so 2SLS with it would be badly biased toward OLS with invalid conventional inference. I will therefore not present a 2SLS effect of graduation as the headline result; the one cleanly identified estimate is the randomized reduced form (ITT) of preschool_assign on voting 1998-2008, estimated with wave/birth_year fixed effects and the baseline covariates (female, iq_entry, parent_educ, father_home, ses_index) for precision, and framed honestly as the effect of the preschool program, not of graduation. As a secondary, clearly labeled analysis of graduation itself, I will use credit_waiver in its subsample with Anderson-Rubin weak-instrument-robust confidence sets (expecting them to be wide or unbounded) and report covariate- and preschool_assign-adjusted OLS of voting on graduation as descriptive only. The roughly 300 generic administrative variables (hot-deck imputed, missing before a 2013 migration, nominal-dollar, post-treatment) are irrelevant or post-treatment for a 1962-65 cohort and will not be used as instruments or controls. The main threat is that the graduation effect is not point-identified in these data because the strong instrument fails exclusion and the valid one is too weak, with secondary concerns that probabilistic name/date-of-birth voter-file matching mismeasures the outcome and that 123 observations leave very little power.

CANDIDATES:
preschool_assign | violated
credit_waiver | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

**Plan**

I would not build the main design on an instrument, because neither candidate supports a credible IV for the effect of high school graduation on turnout: `preschool_assign` is a clean lottery with a strong first stage (19 pp), but the documentation shows it also raised psychosocial skills (teacher ratings at ages 7-9), and a separate experiment shows those skills alone raise turnout by 11-14 pp, so the exclusion restriction fails and a Wald/2SLS estimate would load preschool's direct civic effect onto the graduation coefficient. `credit_waiver` is a lottery whose exclusion restriction is credible ("changed nothing else"), but a 4 pp first stage, F of about 2, and a universe limited to 1965-wave students who reached 12th grade (a few dozen at most) make 2SLS badly biased toward OLS and Anderson-Rubin confidence sets effectively unbounded, so it cannot deliver an informative estimate. The credible estimand the data do support is the intent-to-treat effect of `preschool_assign` on voting 1998-2008 (difference in means with randomization inference given n = 123, adjusted for `female`, `iq_entry`, `parent_educ`, `father_home`, `ses_index`, `birth_year`), which I would report as the headline result and clearly label as the preschool effect, not the graduation effect. For the graduation question I would report the preschool Wald ratio only as an upper bound on the graduation effect (valid if the direct psychosocial channel raises turnout, as the documentation indicates), next to a selection-on-observables estimate using the baseline covariates plus `preschool_assign` as controls, framed as descriptive and accompanied by sensitivity bounds (Oster, Cinelli-Hazlett). Key variables: outcome = voted in at least one general election 1998-2008; treatment = graduated by age 19; `preschool_assign` and `credit_waiver` as the only exogenous shocks; the six entry-time covariates as controls; the roughly 300 agency variables (`welfar_*`, `arrest_*`, `earnin_*`, etc.) are post-treatment, inconsistently documented, and should not enter any specification. Main threat: the graduation effect is not point-identified here because the strong instrument violates exclusion and the valid instrument is too weak, and a secondary threat is outcome misclassification from name-and-birthdate voter-file matching, since false non-matches (movers, name changes) plausibly correlate with graduation and would bias any estimate.

CANDIDATES:
preschool_assign | violated
credit_waiver | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

I will estimate the return to schooling by 2SLS in the full ~330,000-man sample, instrumenting years of completed schooling with qob1 (born January–March) and including year-of-birth and state-of-birth fixed effects, following the Angrist–Krueger logic that school-entry rules plus leave-at-16 laws force first-quarter births to complete about 0.13 fewer years, a first stage that with this sample size is well above weak-instrument thresholds. The key variables are log weekly wage in 1979 (outcome), years of schooling (treatment), qob1 (instrument), year of birth and birth_state (fixed effects), and black as a predetermined control; married, smsa, and region are 1980 outcomes that may themselves respond to schooling, so they enter only as a robustness check, and age_1980 must not be included alongside year-of-birth effects because integer age on April 1, 1980 is a deterministic function of year of birth and qob1 and would absorb the instrument. building_draw is attractive on exclusion grounds (a random 1944 county draw that changed nothing but the school), but it exists only for 1939 births in 20 rural counties of one state, shifts schooling by just 0.03 years, and has a first-stage F of about 2, so 2SLS with it would be biased toward OLS with uninformative intervals; I will report it only as a supplementary Anderson–Rubin check. None of the remaining codebook items (commute, earnings, disability, military, housing, etc.) is a credible instrument: they are functions of the outcome or post-treatment behaviors, and their documentation (2013 system migration, 2014 vendor change, odd-year collection) is inconsistent with a 1980 census extract, so they play no role in the design. The main threat is the exclusion restriction for qob1: quarter of birth is weakly correlated with family background, season-of-birth health, and within-cohort age/experience, and because the first stage is only 0.13 years any direct effect of first-quarter birth on wages is magnified roughly eightfold in the 2SLS estimate (the Bound–Jaeger critique), which I will probe with reduced-form balance checks on predetermined traits and placebo tests in states/cohorts where compulsory-attendance laws did not bind. The resulting estimate is a LATE for compliers at the compulsory-schooling dropout margin, not an average return, and will be interpreted as such.

CANDIDATES:
qob1 | plausible
building_draw | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: qob1

**Plan.** The natural design is instrumental variables for years of schooling on log weekly wage, and the codebook offers two candidate instruments: qob1 (quarter of birth, with year-of-birth and state-of-birth fixed effects) and building_draw (the 1944 random county draw for a consolidated high school). I reject qob1 despite its usable first stage (0.13 fewer years for first-quarter births) because the codebook itself documents that January–March births are disproportionately to teenage and unmarried mothers, so quarter of birth moves wages through family background and not only through schooling, which is a direct violation of the exclusion restriction. building_draw is genuinely randomized and the draw "changed nothing else," so independence and exclusion are plausible, but it shifts schooling by only 0.03 years with a first-stage F of about 2 in a tiny subsample (men born in 1939 in 20 rural counties of one state), so 2SLS would be biased toward OLS and Anderson–Rubin confidence sets for the return to schooling would be essentially unbounded; I will not report it as an IV estimate of the schooling return. Instead, the primary causal analysis is the lottery's reduced form: compare log weekly wage (and schooling) between drawn and undrawn counties for the eligible 1939 cohort, with randomization inference over the 20 counties, interpreted as the intention-to-treat effect of the school-building program, accompanied by OLS of log weekly wage on schooling with black, year-of-birth and state-of-birth controls (married, smsa and region treated as post-treatment and excluded from the main specification) labelled explicitly as descriptive, plus the qob1 reduced form only as a sensitivity exercise with the maternal-background bias direction discussed. Key variables are log weekly wage (outcome), years of schooling (treatment), building_draw (randomized exposure), qob1 (rejected instrument), age_1980/year of birth, birth_state and black (pre-treatment controls); the commut_/earnin_/disabi_/etc. variables describe a 2013–2015 agency case-management system unrelated to the 1980 census and are not candidates for anything. The main threat is power: with 20 counties and F ≈ 2 the lottery design is unbiased but likely uninformative about the magnitude of the return to schooling, so the honest result may be that this dataset cannot deliver a credible point estimate of the schooling return, rather than a weak-IV estimate that merely reproduces OLS.

CANDIDATES:
qob1 | violated
building_draw | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: NONE

The only two variables in the codebook that carry exogenous variation are the two random draws, and neither supports a credible instrumental-variables estimate of the effect of graduating by age 19 on voting in 1998–2008. preschool_assign is randomized with a strong first stage (19 pp), but it violates the exclusion restriction because two years of preschool plausibly affects adult turnout through cognitive and noncognitive skills, earnings, and criminal-justice contact rather than only through graduation; credit_waiver is plausibly valid (random draw, "changed nothing else") but is far too weak to use (4 pp first stage, F ≈ 2) within a sub-sample of roughly 20 seniors from the 1965 wave, so 2SLS would be badly biased toward OLS and a weak-IV-robust Anderson–Rubin set would be essentially unbounded. I will therefore not instrument graduation; the credible design is the preschool randomization itself, estimating the intent-to-treat effect of preschool_assign on the voting indicator (reduced form) together with the first stage on graduation, with balance checks on female, iq_entry, parent_educ, father_home, ses_index and birth_year, wave (birth_year) fixed effects, and randomization inference given n = 123. I will show the ratio of reduced form to first stage only as a transparently labeled "bundled preschool effect per induced graduate," which equals the graduation effect only under the exclusion restriction I have argued fails, and I will report the credit_waiver Anderson–Rubin confidence set to document that the valid instrument is uninformative rather than omit it. OLS of voting on graduation with the baseline covariates and preschool_assign as controls will appear only as a descriptive benchmark, and none of the hundreds of post-entry administrative "items" variables (imputed, suppressed, top-coded, or anchored to a 2013–2015 system that postdates the outcome window) will enter the design as controls or instruments. The main threat is that this design identifies the effect of preschool, not of graduation per se, so the PI's question is not point-identified in these data; a secondary threat is outcome mismeasurement from name-and-date-of-birth voter-file matching, which may differ by graduation status (graduates likely have more stable records and higher match rates) and bias any graduation–voting comparison upward.

CANDIDATES:
preschool_assign | violated
credit_waiver | plausible
INSTRUMENT: NONE
